title: FIDO correctness and whole USB-device trust are separate claims
summary: A physical peripheral can implement a correct FIDO2 authenticator while exposing other USB or radio capabilities. FIDO protocol success therefore does not prove that the surrounding device exposes only the expected authenticator personality. Qualification of a security-key-shaped device must cover the complete observable peripheral personality over time.
invariants: FIDO2 protocol conformance is not a proof that the physical device has no additional interfaces or radios.
A security-key-shaped enclosure, potting, printed antenna or familiar component appearance is weak assurance of runtime personality.
For the transparent Virtual USB hardware target, the expected USB descriptor/interface set must be declared and reproducible.
Unexpected keyboard/mouse, mass-storage, network, display/video, serial or vendor interfaces are qualification failures unless explicitly declared as part of the intended product.
Qualification must observe re-enumeration and generation changes rather than assuming the first descriptor tree remains permanent.
RF capability and firmware provenance are separate hardware-assurance surfaces; FIDO attestation must not be misrepresented as certifying them.
Threat analysis remains defensive; the sphere does not provide an optimized design recipe for covert composite peripherals.
procedure: Record the complete expected descriptor tree and interface classes for the intended hardware release.
Capture and compare descriptors from power-on through re-enumeration/reset cycles.
Fail closed on undeclared interfaces or personality changes.
Retain source/build/firmware hashes and, for higher assurance, hardware/RF inspection evidence separately from FIDO protocol evidence.

provenance.claim: Current intended development personality explicitly declares the FIDO HID interface and endpoints.
README separates FIDO development behavior from production security/certification claims.
